source.title: Why do Learning Rates Transfer? Reconciling Optimization and Scaling Limits for Deep Learning
source.authors: Lorenzo Noci; Alexandru Meterez; Thomas Hofmann; Antonio Orvieto

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures sharpness and training loss during full-batch training near the edge of stability, bearing on V5's stability-threshold dynamics. It does not test the other claim versions' training-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports other CIFAR-10 training losses, but they do not measure classification error or V1–V4/V6 behavior. Cited findings from prior work are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: Appendix B.4 repeats full-batch gradient descent with sharpness and training-loss tracking, explicitly following Cohen et al. (2021), and tests V5's edge-of-stability component under µP. Its linear-network analysis also bears on when that component holds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the full-batch appendix finding but understates the paper's main conclusion. The authors find that leading Hessian eigenvalues can evolve consistently across model sizes under µP and suitable Depth-µP settings, and relate this Super Consistency to learning-rate transfer and feature learning. They do not claim that all parameterizations or all training phases remain near EoS; late-time dynamics and multi-layer residual blocks provide exceptions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies sharpness and learning-rate transfer across scaling parameterizations; its full-batch experiment uses µP and tracks sharpness and loss, rather than testing the original catapult intervention or training-error claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Scaling parameterization, width and depth, learning rate, batch size, warmup, data augmentation, and residual-block layers per block affect sharpness dynamics or transfer. In particular, the paper reports width-dependent late-time sharpness drops and imperfect transfer for some multi-layer residual-block settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Super Consistency of Hessian spectra correlates with learning-rate transfer across widths and depths, whereas loss and NTK spectra accumulate finite-size effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under suitable feature-learning parameterizations, curvature dynamics remain consistent across model sizes and accompany learning-rate transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Disabling residual connections in µP ConvNets makes deeper models harder to train, with vanishing curvature and signal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections affect depth-dependent trainability under µP; this experiment does not establish V3's specified batch-normalized training-error comparison.

record.problems: The full-batch result is shown in figures without numerical sharpness or loss values, error bars, or uncertainty estimates. It is a µP CIFAR-10 subset experiment and does not test the above-initial-limit catapult or larger-rate divergence portions of V5.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization on that error.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their removal by extra student neurons.
The specified comparison of plain batch-normalized networks with identity-shortcut networks; deep tanh initialization and Fixup alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and initialization-dependent trainable depth.
Recovery after exceeding the initial linearized stability limit, the associated initial loss rise and curvature drop, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite starting below the threshold.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup comparison.

missing.what: The full-batch linear-network analysis shows that NTP loses progressive sharpening as width increases and has fixed sharpness in the infinite-width limit.
missing.locator: Section 5, Implications for NTP; Section 4.1 and Figure 5.

missing.what: Proposition 5.3 bounds convergence sharpness between 2/η0 and 2/η0 + η0γ²||w*||²/(ND), conditional on convergence to a marginally stable solution. Under µP the bound is width-independent. This conditional result should be recorded without treating marginal stability or finite-time threshold hovering as proved.
missing.locator: Section 5, Proposition 5.3 and Implications for µP; Appendix C.2.2.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. Stochastic-training departures from EoS are not automatically counterexamples to V5's full-batch statement. Figure-only outcomes support qualitative judgments; the supplied text does not establish numerical loss reductions or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, label corruption, model size, and stopping or regularization effects.
Spurious minima and the effect of student width in teacher-student ReLU problems.
Plain versus shortcut network training error and the effects of special initialization or normalization removal.
Initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth.

The paper does not test the catapult claim that loss briefly rises after exceeding the initial linearized stability limit, nor map divergence at larger rates. Its full-batch CIFAR-10 experiment reports sharpness around the EoS threshold and falling training loss.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: Residual ConvNets
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with µP on a 5000-sample CIFAR-10 subset; sharpness tracked during training.
rows.locator: Appendix B.4, Figure 9 (middle); Appendix C, Figure 9 caption
rows.note: The authors state that sharpness has the typical oscillations around the EoS threshold; Figure 9 plots separate width curves, without numerical values.
rows.check: The plotted quantity is the largest eigenvalue of the scaled Hessian γ²H, compared with 2/η0. Figure 9's legend gives η0=0.769775; its caption rounds this to 0.76. The caption also lists batch size 256 despite describing full-batch GD on 5000 examples; retain this as an unresolved reporting inconsistency, not a confirmed optimization batch size. The EoS statement is in Appendix B.4; Figure 9 is printed within Appendix C.

rows.locator: Appendix B.4, Figure 9 (right); Appendix C, Figure 9 caption
rows.note: Figure 9 plots separate width curves. The text describes the training loss as continuing to decrease in this EoS regime, with a wider-is-better behavior; no numerical values are stated.
